facts.text: Enter the glass doors, turn right through a second set of glass doors and check in at the front desk. Group tours require two weeks’ notice; tours for groups of people with disabilities are free.
facts.quote: You will enter the glass doors and turn right, moving through another set of glass doors. Please proceed to the front desk to check-in. Accessible restrooms are located on all floors except the lobby. All floors are accessible via elevators. There are two elevators available to visitors. A large elevator is located to the left of the visitor services desk and offers access to all gallery floors. Another smaller elevator is located to the right in the lobby and offers access to all gallery floors and the lower level lobby. Service dogs and ponies are welcome. A service animal is defined as any animal that has been trained to do work or performs tasks for the benefit of a person with a disability. Accommodations/Services All of the following are available free of charge at the front desk: Wheelchairs Stools Hearing amplifiers Large print text for exhibitions Reading glasses Magnifiers Sensory bags (fidgets, hearing protection, sensory narrative , and sensory map) Any of the sensory bag objects are also available individually. All of the following are available with two weeks notice : American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation for all public programs. Audio-described tours of the architecture and/or exhibitions. Tours for groups. All tours for groups of individuals with disabilities are free of charge.

facts.text: The current admission page lists $12 general admission, with free admission for members, visitors 18 and under, and SNAP/EBT recipients. Check current eligibility and ticket arrangements.
facts.quote: General Admission $12 CAC Members FREE 18 and Under FREE SNAP/EBT Recipients FREE

facts.text: Bags containing medical equipment and diaper bags are permitted in the galleries; CAC asks visitors to be mindful of their surroundings.
facts.quote: Diaper bags and bags containing medical equipment are permitted in the galleries, but we ask visitors be mindful of their surroundings while exploring the galleries.

facts.text: Gallery floors may close during exhibition changes. Call 513-345-8400 or check the exhibition page for what is currently on view.
facts.quote: CAC is a non-collecting institution, and gallery floors may be closed while exhibitions are changed out. Call us at (513) 345-8400 or visit the Exhibition page to learn about current exhibitions on view.

facts.text: The museum lists ramps, elevators, lifts, accessible restrooms and wheelchairs. Ask the admissions team for a wheelchair or lift assistance.
facts.quote: Accessibility and Accommodations The museum is accessible to visitors with limited mobility, by providing wheelchairs, elevators and lifts, restrooms, parking, and ramps. The Taft also offers sensory accommodations including a quiet room, noise-reducing headphones, and braille and large-print materials to explore the museum collection and exhibitions. Questions? Contact accessibility@taftmuseum.org .

facts.text: A quiet room and noise-reducing headphones are available. Admissions provides Braille and large-print visitor materials.
facts.quote: The Taft also offers sensory accommodations including a quiet room, noise-reducing headphones, and braille and large-print materials to explore the museum collection and exhibitions.

facts.text: The museum's carry-in policy permits water for medical purposes; otherwise outside food and drink are prohibited.
facts.quote: Outside food or drink. Water is allowed only for medical purposes.

facts.text: Wheelchairs, adaptive strollers and other mobility aids are always allowed throughout the museum. Free on-site parking is limited.
facts.quote: Wheelchairs, adaptive strollers, and other mobility aids are always permitted throughout the museum.

facts.text: Large-print exhibition labels are available, and staff are trained to respond to visitors with neurodivergent and invisible disabilities.
facts.quote: KultureCity , a nationally recognized accessibility organization, has provided the Taft team with training and space accommodations to be ready to respond to visitors with neurodivergent and invisible disability needs. To learn more, visit KultureCity's website or app .

facts.text: Bags smaller than 11 by 15 inches can be carried in the galleries.
facts.quote: Backpacks, packages, diaper bags, and laptop bags smaller than 11 x 15 inches may be carried in the galleries.

facts.text: Accessibility questions go to accessibility@taftmuseum.org.
facts.quote: Questions? Contact accessibility@taftmuseum.org .

facts.text: The museum says it is Cincinnati's first Sensory Inclusive certified museum. Flash and phone flashlights are not allowed in the galleries.
facts.quote: The Taft Museum of Art is Cincinnati's first Sensory Inclusive™ certified museum.

facts.text: Segways and other non-medical mobility devices are not permitted. The front gates and garage open 15 minutes before the museum opens.
facts.quote: Segways or other non-medical mobility devices will not be permitted.

facts.text: The coatroom and lockers are on the first floor. Coats must be worn or left in the coatroom; backpacks must be carried by hand or worn on the front.
facts.quote: Bag Policy Backpacks, packages, diaper bags, and laptop bags smaller than 11 x 15 inches may be carried in the galleries. Backpacks may be carried by hand or worn on the front. Coatroom and Lockers The coatroom and lockers are located on the first floor. Your coat may not be carried through the galleries. Please plan on wearing your coat or leave it in the coatroom.

facts.text: The museum is cashless and accepts credit cards, debit cards and other digital payment options.
facts.quote: We are a cashless museum. We accept credit, debit cards, and other digital payment options.

facts.text: Diaper-changing stations are in bathrooms on both the first and second floors. The page does not describe adult-changing equipment or table limits.
facts.quote: Diaper changing stations are available in the bathrooms on both the first and second floors of the museum.

facts.text: The city says Connector vehicles are 100 percent low-floor, with the streetcar floor level with the curb for wheelchairs, scooters and other wheeled devices.
facts.quote: It is one of only two systems in the country to feature 100 percent low-floor streetcar vehicles. This means the floor of the streetcar is level with the curb, allowing quick access for wheeled vehicles (bicycles, strollers, wheelchairs, scooters and personal shopping carts).

facts.text: Riders using wheelchairs, scooters and other mobility aids are directed to board through the center double doors.
facts.quote: Persons with disabilities who use wheelchairs, scooters and other mobility aids should enter through the center double doors.

facts.text: The city lists audio announcements, visual aids such as Braille, and designated seating for people with disabilities.
facts.quote: Audio announcements and visual aids such as Braille and designated seating for individuals with disabilities, make the Connector accessible for all.

facts.text: The city says Metro Access paratransit rides are fare-free when both origin and destination are within 3/4 mile of the Connector route; Access information is available at 513-632-7586.
facts.quote: If your origin and destination is within ¾ mile of the Connector's route, your ride on Access is also fare free! Visit https://www.go-metro.com/accessibility/access-program or call 513-632-7586 for more information on how to use Access.

facts.text: Wheelchairs and other mobility devices are not strapped down; use the designated area and set your brake.
facts.quote: Wheelchairs and other mobility devices don't require securement on the streetcar; please use the designated area and set your brake

facts.text: Cross the tracks at a right angle in a wheelchair or other mobility device, because wheels can catch in the track gap.
facts.quote: People using wheelchairs and other mobility devices should cross the tracks at a right angle. Be careful - wheels can get caught in the track gap

facts.text: Streetcars are very quiet; the city advises crossing only at signalized crosswalks.
facts.quote: Stop and look - streetcars are very quiet... cross only at designated crosswalks with signals

facts.text: The streetcar is free. Real-time arrivals are in the Transit App, and only service animals may ride unless a pet is in a secured carrier.
facts.quote: How much does it cost to ride the Connector? The streetcar is free to ride! Is there an app to see when the next streetcar will arrive? Yes, there is an app. Download the Transit App to plan your trip using real-time GPS monitoring. How accessible is the streetcar? The Connector is fully accessible to people with disabilities. Vehicles have level-floor boarding and audio and visual messages for all riders. The floor of the streetcar is level with the station, allowing quick access for wheeled vehicles including bicycles, strollers, wheelchairs, scooters, luggage and personal shopping carts. Persons with disabilities who use wheelchairs, scooters and other mobility aids should enter through the center double doors. Are pets allowed onboard? Only service animals are allowed on the streetcar. No other pets are allowed on the streetcar unless they are in a secured pet carrier.

facts.text: Each streetcar has 38 seats and room for 116 standing riders.
facts.quote: Each streetcar weighs 40 tons empty and can carry 38 seated and 116 standing, for a total of 154 passengers.

facts.text: Press the red stop button as your stop approaches to tell the operator you want to exit. The city’s riding instructions identify this as the exit-request procedure.
facts.quote: When approaching your stop, press the red stop button to signal to the operator that you are ready to exit.

facts.text: The city says route maps are posted inside every streetcar and links an online route map for choosing a destination. This does not establish the approach to an individual platform.
facts.quote: Check the route map here to determine your desired destination. Maps also are posted inside every streetcar.

facts.text: The Rules of the Rail direct riders to the onboard intercom to contact the operator in an emergency. Other communication formats or intercom reach are not specified.
facts.quote: In an emergency, use intercom to contact operator.

facts.text: Small personal grocery carts are permitted onboard; grocery-store carts are excluded. Riders may bring luggage they can control, and strollers do not have to be folded.
facts.quote: Small, personal grocery carts (not grocery store carts) Bikes -- walk bike on and off the streetcar and hold onto your bike at all times Strollers do not have to be folded Luggage that you can control

facts.text: The posted rules prohibit open containers of food or drinks. The page does not describe a medical exception; ask the operator about particular needs before travel.
facts.quote: No open containers of food or drinks.

facts.text: The arboretum says there are several places to leave the paved trail for woodland trails; those side trails are not described as paved.
facts.quote: Scattered around the grounds are several opportunities to leave the paved trail and explore the local forest.

facts.text: The arboretum’s About page describes a 2.2-mile paved multi-use trail connecting its collections. This is its published distance, not a measured route or gradient assessment.
facts.quote: There are currently over 5,500 trees and shrubs in our collection, and a variety of annual and perennial flower displays, all connected by a paved 2.2-mile multi-use trail.

facts.text: The arboretum’s About page lists daily hours of 7:30 a.m. to dusk and no admission or parking charge.
facts.quote: We are open daily from 7:30am to dusk, and there is no charge for admission or parking.

facts.text: The visit-planning page describes year-round dawn-to-dusk opening, with free parking and admission and no residency requirement.
facts.quote: As a public facility, the Boone County Arboretum grounds are open from dawn until dusk, every day of the year, with no charge for parking or admission. No county/state residency requirement - visitors from all around are welcome.

facts.text: Four information kiosks provide brochures, maps and event information. Printed visitor guides and plant maps are available in the kiosks; the visit-planning page also links PDF and interactive maps. Kiosk reach and print formats are not specified.
facts.quote: Four informational kiosks spaced throughout the property provide brochures, maps and event information. A general map of the facility layout and additional details can be found in the official Visitor's Guide. Printed copies are available in the kiosks, or download a pdf version . Our plant collection contains over 3600 individual trees and woody shrubs in more than 25 collection areas. The entire plant collection has been inventoried and mapped. You can search our inventory online multiple ways. Printed maps are available in the kiosks, or as a pdf download . You can also browse our web-based interactive map .

facts.text: The visit-planning page says over two miles of paved walking and bicycling trails interconnect the gardens, wildlife-viewing area, restrooms and sports facilities. It gives no slopes, widths, restroom features or seasonal opening details.
facts.quote: Features of interest include a children's garden, a butterfly garden, and a wildlife viewing area surrounded by a native grassland. An example rain garden and an overhead utility planting demonstration area. There are also restrooms, baseball and soccer fields, tennis and basketball courts. These features are all interconnected by over two miles of paved walking / bicycling trails.

facts.text: The arboretum publishes its contact address as 9190 Camp Ernst Road, Union, KY 41091. Confirm the destination with the arboretum if your navigation service uses a different postal label.
facts.quote: 9190 Camp Ernst Road, Union, KY 41091

facts.text: New Riff says there are no stairs leading to the distillery’s front door. Door controls, thresholds and the complete route from parking are not described.
facts.quote: There are no stairs leading to the front door and our large elevator has plenty of room for wheelchairs and anyone assisting.

facts.text: The distillery describes a large elevator for wheelchair users and companions. It publishes no car or door dimensions here; contact the venue about particular arrangements.
facts.quote: There are no stairs leading to the front door and our large elevator has plenty of room for wheelchairs and anyone assisting. If you have any specific concerns or accommodations you can always give us a call!

facts.text: A free parking lot is directly in front of the distillery. The FAQ does not identify designated spaces, a drop-off point or a measured parking-to-door route.
facts.quote: Is there parking available at the distillery? Yes, there is a free parking lot directly in front of the building.

facts.text: The gift shop and Aquifer tasting room accept walk-ins during business hours; you do not need to take a tour to visit them.
facts.quote: Do I need a tour to visit the distillery? No. Our gift shop and Aquifer tasting room are both open to visitors and walk-ins during business hours.

facts.text: Tours, tastings and classes are restricted to guests aged 21 or over. The experiences FAQ separately welcomes children in the gift shop and visitor center.
facts.quote: Children are welcome in our gift shop and visitor center. Guests participating on distillery tours, tastings or classes must be of legal drinking age (21 years old and up).

facts.text: The Bonded Tour at 24 Distillery Way is listed as 45–60 minutes. It follows the distilling process; the page does not specify seated rest stops or an option to shorten the route.
facts.quote: 45 - 60 minutes Tue: 12pm, 2pm Wed-Fri: 12pm, 2pm, 4pm Sat: 12pm, 2pm, 3pm, 4pm, 5:30pm Sun: 12pm, 2pm, 3pm 24 Distillery Way Newport KY 41073

facts.text: The Aquifer and New Riff Distilling are card-only and accept major credit and debit cards.
facts.quote: Do you accept cash? No. New Riff Distilling and The Aquifer Tasting Room are card only. We accept all major credit and debit cards.

facts.text: The Aquifer lists Monday closure and closures on Easter Sunday, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day and New Year’s Day. Check its current hours before travelling.
facts.quote: Monday: CLOSED Tuesday - Thursday: 11:00 AM - 7:00 PM Friday - Saturday: 11:00 AM - 8:00 PM Sunday: 11:00 AM - 5:00 PM New Riff Distillery 24 Distillery Way Newport, KY 41073 *The Aquifer is closed Easter Sunday, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day and New Year's Day.

facts.text: Check your booking’s destination: West Newport Campus is at 1104 Lowell Street and is available only by tour, experience or appointment. It is separate from this public distillery and Aquifer listing.
facts.quote: New Riff West Newport Campus Home to our rickhouse, bottling line, and historic tasting room, this is where our whiskey ages and comes to life. Experience it through our Barrel Proof Tour, Blend Experience, or Single Barrel Selection. This location is not open to the public and is available by tour, experience, or appointment only. New Riff Distillery 1104 Lowell Street Newport, KY 41071

facts.text: The published cancellation policy allows a full refund up to 72 hours before the booked event. Within 72 hours, the page says no refunds or changes.
facts.quote: Any cancelled booking may be refunded in full up to 72 hours of the event. Within 72 hours, no refund or changes are permitted.

facts.text: Braxton says an elevator serves its second-floor Loft private-event space. The FAQ does not identify the elevator entrance or establish a route to the rooftop.
facts.quote: Yes, we have elevator access to the Loft event space on the second floor that's ADA approved.

facts.text: The Loft FAQ lists four paid parking lots within a block. It does not identify designated spaces or a continuous step-free route from a particular lot.
facts.quote: There are 4 pay parking lots within a block of the venue as well.

facts.text: The main taproom is on the first floor; the Loft is a second-floor private-event space, with a rooftop bar also advertised. These are separate areas to specify when arranging a visit.
facts.quote: This family and dog friendly brewery features an expansive first floor taproom, second floor private event space, and one of Cincinnati's best Rooftop Bars.

facts.text: To reserve a first-floor table, email social@braxtonbrewing.com. The Covington page links a separate rooftop reservation service.
facts.quote: guests can use this link to make a rooftop reservation or email social@braxtonbrewing.com to reserve a table on the first floor.

facts.text: Some restaurant entrances may have a step up. Riverside does not identify those doors or publish a step-free alternative for each stop; discuss the exact itinerary before booking.
facts.quote: There may be a step up to the entrance, at a few of the restaurants.

facts.text: The operator describes less than one mile of walking over three hours, with park benches along the neighborhood route. It does not give rest intervals, gradients or assistance procedures.
facts.quote: We walk less than one mile over the course of 3 hours. This tour is easy due to the level surfaces, tree-lined streets, and park benches.

facts.text: The tour page lists a paid parking lot behind Cedar at 417 W. 7th Street. Designated spaces and the connection to the 701 Main Street meeting point are not described.
facts.quote: There is a pay parking lot behind Cedar Restaurant. The parking lot address is 417 W. 7th Street, Covington KY 41011.

facts.text: The operator says all tour restaurants have public restrooms. Toilet layouts, step-free approaches and changing facilities are not specified.
facts.quote: Are restrooms available? Yes, all the restaurants have public restrooms.

facts.text: Vegetarian dishes can be requested when booking, but Riverside does not guarantee dietary accommodations at every stop. Call or text 513-289-0035 in advance to discuss options.
facts.quote: Vegetarian dishes are available upon booking. We do our best to accommodate dietary needs, but we cannot guarantee it at every stop. Please call or text 513-289-0035 in advance to discuss your options.

facts.text: The tour runs in hot, cold or rainy weather, with about 70% indoors according to the operator. Severe-weather cancellation or rescheduling is communicated by text or email.
facts.quote: Our tours run rain or shine, in hot or cold weather. Since about 70% of the tour takes place indoors, we limit outdoor time as much as possible during inclement weather. Please dress for the conditions. In the case of severe or life-threatening weather, we will contact you by text or email if a tour must be canceled or rescheduled.

facts.text: Booking confirmation is emailed with directions and the meeting point. A printed ticket is unnecessary if you received the confirmation.
facts.quote: You will receive an e-mail containing booking details, directions and meeting point information. It is not necessary to print the ticket as long as you received an email confirmation.

facts.text: Riverside does not accept walk-up or cash ticket sales. Arrange the booking before arriving.
facts.quote: Can I just arrive and pay? Walk up or cash sales are not accepted.

facts.text: The tour advertises a stop at the 40-foot German clock tower. This identifies a neighborhood landmark, not a current clock or chime operating schedule.
facts.quote: The 40-ft German clock tower Marvel at the 40-ft German clock tower , and discover the scandalous tale of the only governor ever murdered in U.S. history .

facts.text: The park has 2.35 miles of paved walking trails, plus concession and restroom buildings; their accessibility is not stated.
facts.quote: Central Park & Arboretum is a 121-acre park in Union with 2.35 miles of paved trails, wooded and open views, sports courts and fields, wetlands, a children's garden and the Arboretum at Central Park. Reserve a shelter and stay awhile. facts.text: Additional clause of taft-museum-of-art.mobility.1
facts.quote: If you need a wheelchair or assistance with a lift, ask the Visitor Experience team at admissions.

facts.text: Additional clause of taft-museum-of-art.mobility.2
facts.quote: The Taft offers limited, free on-site parking for guests visiting the museum, the Museum Shop, and the Taft Café during regular museum hours in the Taft's on-site garage.

facts.text: Additional clause of taft-museum-of-art.sensory.2
facts.quote: Large print versions of these resources and exhibition labels are also available.

facts.text: Additional clause of taft-museum-of-art.sensory.3
facts.quote: Photography encouraged, but please no flash or flashlights! Take a selfie or snap a picture of your favorite artwork, but protect the art by refraining from using flash or your smartphone's flashlight.

facts.text: Additional clause of taft-museum-of-art.mobility.3
facts.quote: The front gates and garage open 15 minutes before museum opening.

facts.text: Additional clause of taft-museum-of-art.chronic.3
facts.quote: Backpacks may be carried by hand or worn on the front.

facts.text: Entry directions retained in revised note
facts.quote: You will enter the glass doors and turn right, moving through another set of glass doors. Please proceed to the front desk to check-in.
